articleTitle: Measured performance of a broadband matching section for peripherally fed helical antennas
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes the measured performance of an impedance matching section incorporated into the first turn of a peripherally fed helical antenna to transform its impedance to 50 Ω. The design of the matching section is briefly reviewed. The measured results show that very low VSWR (1,2:1) can be achieved over the usable frequency range of the antenna. In addition to showing the basic impedance matching performance, results are also presented to illustrate the effect of the number of helix turns and of the conductor diameter on the impedance match. Antenna pattern data show that improved performance can be achieved by a simple termination at the free end of the helix.

articleTitle: A method for the prediction of earth-space rain-attenuation distribution in the USA, using a southern African rain-rate model
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Results of rain-attenuation prediction on earth-satellite paths in the USA, utilizing a rain-rate model based on southern African extreme rain-rate data, are presented. The model, based on Lin's extreme-value theory, was used to provide 5-minute rain-rate distributions. These were then used in an existing attenuation model to provide the attenuation distributions for a total of 16 earth-space paths, at frequencies of 11 to 29 GHz. Good agreement with the experimental distributions is obtained over a range of climates. These results, together with earlier results obtained with the prediction of 5-min rain-rate distributions in the USA, have brought about a high degree of confidence in the method for rain-attenuation prediction. The method should be useful, not only for the continental USA, but also for southern Africa. The method is easy to use. The rain-rate model requires only the mean annual rainfall and a designation of the location as climatically coastal or inland.

articleTitle: The effects of lightning on pulse code modulation (PCM) transmission systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An investigation has been carried out to determine the effect of lightning on the performance of Pulse Code Modulation (PCM)telecommunication systems. The present protection used on PCM systems is described and the effects of surge conditions on system performance are identified.

articleTitle: Travelling ionospheric disturbances and their effects on high-frequency direction finding
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A model, which has been shown to represent TIDs reasonably realistically for ray tracing at near-vertical incidence, has been used in a computer simulation of HF signals under disturbed conditions. The variation in angles of arrival, signal strength, and frequency, for transmitters separated by about 300 km from a receiver at Johannesburg, is calculated for a 10 MHz signal at two phases of disturbances with two different vertical extents. A detailed explanation is given, linking the variations in the parameters of the received signal to the physical effects of the TID. It is shown that the accuracy of position location can be improved by taking ionospheric variability into account.

articleTitle: Measurements of surges on underground telephone cables
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A novel type of field surge monitor developed at the Post Office Telectronic Institute is described. Some results obtained using these monitors are given.

articleTitle: Induction motor behaviour in the presence of unbalanced supply voltages
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes an investigation into the derating of induction motors supplied from unbalanced three phase voltages.

articleTitle: A compact, aperture-matched, balanced transmission line antenna+
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes a novel balanced transmission line antenna where the maximum separation between the two conductors is only a fraction of a wavelength at the lowest operating frequency. The balanced transmission line is formed by exponentially extending the ridges of a double-ridged waveguide. The poor VSWR and patterns caused by reflections from the tips of the ridge extensions are improved by a combination of aperture matching and the use of microwave absorber. Measured VSWR, radiation pattern and gain data are presented for this compact, broadband antenna over the 2 to 11 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: The dynamic performance of fast digitisers used for recording non-repetitive signals
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The dynamic performance of fast digitisers is discussed in this paper in an attempt to answer the fundamental question: “What is the maximum instantaneous error in the recorded digital waveform of a fast non-repetitive impulse?”.

articleTitle: Ionospheric propagation from Sanae, Antarctica, to Grahamstown, South Africa
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper reports an analysis of hourly oblique ionograms made in a winter month (August 1975) and a summer month (January 1976) between Sanae and Grahamstown. The maximum observed frequency (MOF) and the lowest observed frequency on the low-angle ray (LLOF) were scaled, and inverse transmission curves were used to estimate the equivalent vertical frequency (EVFO) for the ordinary ray. The data are used to show the frequency ranges and times of day for which transmission in the different modes may be expected.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic propagation underground with special reference to mining
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The mechanisms by which electromagnetic energy may propagate underground are identified and discussed. Particular attention is paid to the work done in this field in South Africa over the last thirty years by presenting both theoretical and experimental results over a range of frequencies from mf to UHF. The results of similar investigations conducted by workers in other countries are cited and fairly good correlation between the various theories and the experimental data is shown to exist at both extremes of frequency. Guided modes are shown to be of major importance, with natural stratification and incidental guiding structures playing significant roles.

articleTitle: An algorithm for detecting loss of synchronisation in data transmission test sets
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Tests on high-speed hf data channels, using transmission test sets which are designed for channels with low error rates, showed that a false indication of a loss of synchronisation was frequently recorded during long error bursts. An algorithm is described whereby the probability of such a false decision can be calculated and set to any acceptable value in a test receiver, while a true loss of synchronisation will be detected within a specified number of data bits.
